turns.content: State the karyotypic abnormalities in Klinefelter and Down syndromes.
Compare chromosome-wide dosage compensation of the extra X in XXY with the absence of analogous chromosome-21 silencing.
Describe the post-zygotic chromatin mechanism that largely inactivates the supernumerary X.
Identify the molecular process that most directly buffers the established XXY state relative to trisomy 21.
Relate repressive chromatin methylation to silencing of the extra X at the same developmental stage.
Explain why post-zygotic dosage compensation, rather than meiotic nondisjunction, addresses the phenotypic contrast.
Derive the mechanistic explanation from karyotype, timing, and chromosome-wide dosage regulation.
Identify how escape genes, incomplete X inactivation, mosaicism, and tissue variation limit uniform dosage compensation in XXY.
Compare the residual dosage imbalance expected in XXY with the chromosome-wide dosage gain in trisomy 21, which lacks analogous silencing.
Synthesize the mechanism and its limitations into an explanation for the phenotypic contrast between Klinefelter and Down syndromes.
